verdict.rationale: Stripe's first-party API docs say the API supports idempotency keys so a request can be safely repeated after a connection error, without creating a second object or performing the update twice. That is the core of the story. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and documented details on key scope across HTTP methods and key retention or expiry needed to confirm 'any' request.

support.subject: As a developer, I can safely retry any API request using idempotency keys so network failures never create duplicate charges

citations.quote: The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice.
use an idempotency key. Then, if a connection error occurs, you can safely repeat the request without risk of creating a second object or performing the update twice.
